_comment: Worked vote arithmetic: one case per line of reasoning that could go wrong. Each case is inputs plus the answer the tally must produce, so the arithmetic is reviewable as data by someone who does not read code. Read by tally.py and by the dashboard's counter, so the two cannot diverge. Thresholds come from docs/data.json; nothing here restates a number the Constitution states.

cases.name: tier-c/exact-threshold-carries
cases.why: Quorum met exactly at 7 of 14, and a majority of 7 is 4. Both boundaries at once.

cases.name: tier-c/quorum-one-short
cases.why: Four beats two, and it still fails: six responders is below the quorum of half of all members.

cases.name: tier-c/tie-fails
cases.why: THE REGRESSION VECTOR. A majority of 14 is 8, because a majority is more than half. Computing ceil(14/2) gives 7 and carries a tied vote.

cases.name: tier-c/dual-denominator
cases.why: THE HEADLINE VECTOR. Carries on four preferences out of fourteen. The four tolerations count toward quorum (11 responders) and are excluded from the majority denominator (7). One denominator for quorum, another for the majority. An implementation using 11 for both would require 6 and fail this.

cases.name: tier-c/zero-denominator
cases.why: Quorum is met and nobody chose preference or objection. A majority of nobody is not a majority.

cases.name: tier-c/objection-only
cases.why: One objection, no preferences. Quorum met; the majority is not.

cases.name: layer-3/exact-eight
cases.why: Majority of all members, so the denominator is the roll and no quorum applies.

cases.name: layer-3/seven-fails
cases.why: Seven of fourteen is half, not a majority. Proves ceil was not used for a majority of all members.

cases.name: layer-3/toleration-trap
cases.why: Every member answered. Nobody objected. It fails. This is the case to show members: toleration is not a yes.

cases.name: layer-4/nine-of-fourteen-fails
cases.why: Two-thirds of 14 rounds up to 10. Nine of fourteen is not two-thirds.

cases.name: layer-4/ten-carries-over-four-objections
cases.why: No objection veto at Layer 4 and no quorum. Ten affirmative is the whole test.

cases.name: layer-4/abstention-equals-non-response
cases.why: Same verdict as four non-responses, and the counts reported must still differ. Keep both words; let the tally bucket them.

cases.name: re-ratification/ten-of-fourteen
cases.why: The vote the Laboratory's continued existence depends on.

cases.name: re-ratification/nine-ends-the-laboratory
cases.why: Fourteen members answered, nobody objected, and the Constitution lapses. Five non-preferences are enough.

cases.name: removal/nine-carries
cases.why: Two-thirds of all members other than the respondent: ceil(13 x 2/3) = 9. The respondent does not vote and is not a non-response.

cases.name: removal/eight-fails
cases.why: One short, on an electorate of thirteen rather than fourteen.

cases.name: remedy/respondent-excluded
cases.why: Two denominators and a reduced electorate together: quorum over half of all other members, the two-thirds over the other members who vote.

cases.name: emergency/no-verdict
cases.why: Section 2 defines 'those who vote' for Tier C only, so the Emergency clause's bare phrase is undetermined. Reading it as preference+objection carries; reading it as all responders fails. Print both and decline.

cases.name: recall/no-verdict
cases.why: Section 3.9 states neither denominator nor quorum. Supplying one would set a threshold, which Section 2 reserves to Layer 4. The gap must stay visible every time anyone runs this.
